scenes.name: the gap is one division
scenes.visual: Dark canvas, three horizontal bands, nothing clears. Top band (y 110–250): the puzzle bar from the thirty-millisecond chapter, at full size: a coral bar from x=210 to x=1710 (1,500 px = 30 ms) with a 5 px amber sliver at its left end. Its two text labels show only during b1; after that the bar keeps just its grey tag '× 300' at the right end. Centre band (y 330–600): an equation that builds term by term: a fraction, amber 'peak' over coral 'bandwidth', then a white '÷', then a white chip '1 op per byte' with a tiny blue token pill on it, then '= ?'. Bottom band (y 680–960): two result rows that fill the equation in with numbers, one per chip, each led by a small GPU package icon and its name. At most five word labels on screen at any moment; the rest are numbers. Colour by meaning: amber arithmetic, coral memory, white results, grey caveats. The idea the motion makes visible: the puzzle's gap is one division, the chip's ridge over the workload's one operation per byte, and its exact size depends on which chip you divide for.

beats.say: Thirty milliseconds a token, and a tenth of one for its arithmetic. That gap is not a mystery. It is a division.
beats.show: On 'thirty milliseconds', the coral bar sweeps from x=210 to x=1710, label '30 ms per token' above its left end. On 'a tenth of one', the 5 px amber sliver lights at its left end, label '0.1 ms arithmetic'. On 'that gap', a grey bracket spans the coral part and the tag '× 300' clicks on at the right end. On 'a division', both text labels fade out, leaving the bar, the sliver and the '× 300' tag, and a white '÷' fades in at centre stage, waiting for its terms.

beats.say: Two hardware numbers, peak arithmetic over bandwidth, make the chip's ridge. Divide by one property of the workload, decode's one operation per byte, and that is the gap.
beats.show: The equation builds centre stage. On 'peak arithmetic', amber 'peak' writes on left of the '÷'; on 'bandwidth', coral 'bandwidth' writes on beneath it with a fraction line; on 'the chip's ridge', a grey bracket under the fraction, label 'ridge'. On 'one property of the workload', the white chip '1 op per byte' slides in right of the '÷', with a grey bracket label 'decode'. On 'that is the gap', '= ?' writes on and a thin white line draws from the '?' up to the '× 300' tag on the bar, which pulses once.

beats.say: Two hundred and ninety-five on an H one hundred. On the H two hundred behind the thirty milliseconds, same arithmetic, faster memory, about two hundred and six. Three hundred came from round numbers.
beats.show: The bracket labels 'ridge' and 'decode' fade. On 'two hundred and ninety-five', the first row writes on in the bottom band: GPU icon 'H100', amber '989' ÷ coral '3.35' ÷ white '1' = white '295', the result counting up, and the white line from '?' re-routes to it. On 'H two hundred', the second row writes on beneath: GPU icon 'H200', amber '989' ÷ coral '4.8' ÷ white '1', with a small stopwatch '29.2 ms' at its right end. On 'same arithmetic', both amber '989's pulse together; on 'faster memory', the coral '4.8' pulses; on 'two hundred and six', its result counts up to '206'. On 'round numbers', the top bar corrects itself at full size: the amber sliver widens from 5 to 7 px under a grey tag '0.1 ms was 0.14', the coral bar's right end trims back to x=1668 under a grey tag '30 ms is the H200', and the '× 300' tag strikes through and rolls to '× 206', tied by a white line to the H200 row's '206'.

scenes.name: the chain, in five links
scenes.visual: New composition. Top-left, a small grey heading 'The chain, in five links' (fades after b1). Left 62% of the frame (x 120–1180): five link cards stacked vertically, each 128 px tall with 40 px gaps (y 150–952), blue outlines, a numbered circle '1' to '5' at the left, a small icon, then the card's title in white. A chain-link icon (two interlocking rings) joins each card to the next. At the right end of each card (x 840–1170) sits its result chip, which carries its own operation so the ÷ or × sign is visible. Right of the stack (x 1280–1800): a large stopwatch reading '30 ms', joined to the whole stack by one tall white bracket running from card 1 to card 5. The card being spoken about is at full brightness; finished cards dim to 60%. Card icons and chips: 1, two vertical arrows drawn to scale, amber 120 px and coral 26 px (80 : 17), chip '80 ÷ 17 ≈ 4.7'; 2, a GPU package with a coral stream on its bus, chip coral '70 bn × 2 bytes = 140 GB'; 3, one coral read stream fanning into a block of blue pills above a second stream feeding one lone pill, chip coral '140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms'; 4, a short stack of blue blocks, chip coral '2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 B ≈ 320 KB'; 5, a funnel, chip teal 'throughput × share on time'. The idea the motion makes visible: five short statements, each carrying one piece of arithmetic, chained into a single explanation of the thirty milliseconds.

beats.say: Five sentences explain the thirty milliseconds. Compute outgrows bandwidth, eighty times against seventeen in a decade, so the ridge climbs. A forward pass streams every weight, a hundred and forty gigabytes a token.
beats.show: On 'five sentences', the heading writes on and the five empty cards fade in, their numbers and chain links drawing top to bottom. On 'the thirty milliseconds', the stopwatch '30 ms' appears at right and its bracket draws down the whole stack. On 'compute outgrows bandwidth', card 1's title writes on; on 'eighty times', its amber arrow grows to full height; on 'seventeen', its coral arrow grows to about a fifth of that; on 'the ridge climbs', chip 1 writes on, '80 ÷ 17 ≈ 4.7'. On 'a forward pass', card 1 dims, the heading fades and card 2's title writes on; on 'every weight', a coral stream runs across its GPU icon's bus; on 'a hundred and forty gigabytes', chip 2 writes on, '70 bn × 2 bytes = 140 GB'.

beats.say: Prefill amortises that read, decode does not: every token pays it in full. The K V cache adds to the bill, three hundred and twenty kilobytes for every token held.
beats.show: Card 2 dims. On 'prefill amortises', card 3's title writes on and its upper stream fans out into the block of blue pills, all lighting at once; on 'decode does not', the lower stream, just as wide, feeds its one lone pill; on 'pays it in full', chip 3 writes on, '140 GB ÷ 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms', and the stopwatch at right ticks once. On 'the K V cache', card 3 dims and card 4's title writes on, its stack of blue blocks growing by one; on 'three hundred and twenty kilobytes', chip 4 builds term by term, '2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 B', then '≈ 320 KB'.

beats.say: And goodput, the tokens that arrive in time, is what is actually sold. Each link is a division or a multiplication you can now do yourself, nothing beyond arithmetic.
beats.show: On 'goodput', card 4 dims and card 5's title writes on; small blue tokens drop into its funnel, those in time passing through teal, late ones bouncing off grey. On 'actually sold', chip 5 writes on in teal, 'throughput × share on time'. On 'a division or a multiplication', all five cards return to full brightness, the camera eases back so the chain and the stopwatch fill the frame, and the signs in the chips light amber one chip after another, top to bottom: the ÷ in chip 1, the × in chip 2, the ÷ in chip 3, the four × in chip 4, the × in chip 5. On 'nothing beyond arithmetic', the bracket from the chain to the stopwatch glows white along its full length and holds.

scenes.name: the road ahead
scenes.visual: New composition. Top band (y 60–230): one division, large and centred, built term by term: white 'tokens per second =', a coral box 'bandwidth', '÷', and a coral box 'bytes per token' that on cue splits into coral 'bytes per read' ÷ blue 'tokens sharing each read'. Each of the three final terms owns a fixed annotation slot directly beneath it (y 240–300): slot A under 'bandwidth' (x 560–900), slot B under 'bytes per read' (x 1000–1360), slot C under 'tokens sharing each read' (x 1440–1840). A slot holds at most one chip; nothing else is placed there. Lower part (y 340–1010): a large rounded blue panel titled 'Where the series goes from here', holding eight cards in a 4 × 2 grid, each with an icon, a label of at most three words and a tiny grey video number in its top corner. Row one: '2 · the accelerator' (a chip icon), '3 · the code on it' (a code-brackets icon), '4 · fewer bits' (a row of sixteen binary digits), '5 · across many chips' (two chip icons joined by a link). Row two: '6 · part of itself' (a pie with one slice lit), '7 · serving at scale' (a crowd of user icons), '8 · idle units in decode' (a sleeping chip with a small 'z'), '9 · one real request' (a route icon). Cards start dimmed to 30%; as each is named it brightens and a thin line draws from it up to the term it moves, coloured like that term. Lines persist, so by the end every card is wired to the division. The idea the motion makes visible: eight later videos, one division, each pulling on one of its terms.

beats.say: That leaves one division: tokens per second is bandwidth over bytes per token, and one read can serve many tokens. Its three terms are the escape routes from earlier.
beats.show: On 'tokens per second', the division writes on term by term: 'tokens per second =', coral 'bandwidth', '÷', coral 'bytes per token'. On 'one read can serve many tokens', the 'bytes per token' box splits into coral 'bytes per read' ÷ blue 'tokens sharing each read'. On 'three terms', a small teal arrow appears beside each term in turn: up beside 'bandwidth', down beside 'bytes per read', up beside 'tokens sharing each read'. On 'from earlier', the panel 'Where the series goes from here' fades in below with its eight dimmed cards.

beats.say: Ahead: the accelerator, the chip itself, and the code on it. Fewer bits per weight. One model across many chips.
beats.show: On 'the accelerator', card 2 brightens and draws a coral line up to 'bandwidth'; slot A shows a coral chip 'H200: 4.8 TB/s → ≈ 34 tokens/s'. On 'the code on it', card 3 brightens and draws a coral line to 'bytes per read', whose arrow pulses. On 'fewer bits', card 4 brightens, its sixteen binary digits shrink to eight, it draws a coral line to 'bytes per read', and slot B shows a coral chip '8-bit: 70 GB → ≈ 48 tokens/s'. On 'many chips', card 5 brightens and draws a coral line to 'bandwidth', whose arrow pulses.

beats.say: Models that use only part of themselves per token. Serving at scale. Decode's idle arithmetic, put to work. And one real request, traced end to end.
beats.show: On 'part of themselves', card 6 brightens and draws a coral line to 'bytes per read'. On 'serving at scale', card 7 brightens and draws a blue line to 'tokens sharing each read'; slot C shows a blue chip '10 users → ≈ 240 tokens/s in all' with a small grey line under it, 'weights only · each user ≈ 24'. On 'idle arithmetic', card 8's sleeping chip wakes, a small amber tag on the card reads '> 99% idle at batch 1', and it draws a blue line to 'tokens sharing each read'. On 'one real request', card 9 brightens; the six-stop route from earlier draws in miniature along the panel's bottom edge (y about 990, beneath row two) as six small icon dots joined by a line, with one blue token pill travelling along it, and three lines from card 9 reach all three terms at once.

beats.say: Each attacks the same division, trying to move one term. Hold that frame, and the series reads as a single argument.
beats.show: All eight cards are at full brightness, each wired to its term. On 'the same division', the division pulses once and every line pulses with it. On 'move one term', each term's teal arrow nudges once in its own direction. On 'a single argument', the eight lines draw together into one bright bundle feeding the division, and the panel dims to 50% so the division and the bundle hold the frame.

scenes.name: closing
scenes.visual: Everything clears to the dark canvas: a quiet, spacious ending. Centre, a single blue token pill beside a stopwatch, a callback to the film's first picture of tokens streaming out. Then two short lines in two colours. Then the end card: the film's title, the series name and what comes next. Slow, unhurried motion; long holds.

beats.say: Arithmetic is cheap. Data movement is expensive.
beats.show: From the clear canvas, a blue token pill settles at centre beside a stopwatch reading '30 ms'; a thin coral stream flows beneath it, left to right, and a tiny amber dot beside the stream blinks once and sits still. On 'arithmetic is cheap', amber 'Arithmetic is cheap.' writes on above the pill; on 'data movement is expensive', coral 'Data movement is expensive.' writes on beneath it. Hold two seconds.

beats.say: Next, inside the G P U. This has been The Memory Wall.
beats.show: The pill, stream and two lines rise and fade. On 'inside the G P U', a small blue card with a chip icon fades in near the bottom: 'Next: Inside the GPU'. On 'The Memory Wall', the title 'The Memory Wall' fades in at centre in large white type, with 'The Engineering Behind LLM Inference · video 1 of 9' beneath it in grey. Hold three seconds after the last word, then fade to black.

checks.claim: Puzzle (as stated in the cold open and ch05): 10^11 ops / 10^15 ops/s = 0.1 ms of arithmetic
Puzzle factor: 30 ms / 0.1 ms = 300 (round numbers)
Puzzle bar: 0.1 ms sliver on a 1,500 px bar for 30 ms is 5 px
Tag '0.1 ms was 0.14': unrounded arithmetic per token = 140e9 / 989e12 = 0.14 ms
Tag '30 ms is the H200' and stopwatch '29.2 ms': 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms
Corrected bar: 0.1416 ms sliver = 7 px; 29.17 ms bar = 1,458 px, so its right end trims from x=1710 to x=1668
Decode intensity: (2 x 70 billion ops) / (70 billion x 2 bytes) = 1 op per byte
Ridge on H100: 989 TFLOP/s / 3.35 TB/s = 295 ops per byte
Ridge on H200: same 989 TFLOP/s dense 16-bit (same compute die; a hardware fact also used in ch17, not stated in the atlas) / 4.8 TB/s = 206 ops per byte
Gap on H100 = memory time / arithmetic time = (140e9/3.35e12) / (140e9/989e12) = 295 = ridge / 1

REVIEWER BLOCKER FIX: gap on the H200 that produced the 30 ms = (140e9/4.8e12) / (140e9/989e12) = 206.04, not 295 and not 300; the puzzle's 300 came from rounding (0.14 ms down to 0.1, 29.2 ms up to 30). ch05 already said 'about two hundred times rather than three' unrounded.
Gap = ridge / decode intensity = (peak / bandwidth) / (ops per byte), for both chips

CORRECTION to fig 146 label 'the factor of 300 = bandwidth / bytes per token': bandwidth / bytes per token is a rate, 23.9 tokens/s on an H100 (the decode ceiling), not a dimensionless factor. The film states the gap as (peak / bandwidth) / (ops per byte) = ridge / intensity: 295 on an H100, 206 on an H200, i.e. two hardware numbers and one property of the workload, as the figure's prose says.
Link 1: compute x80 vs bandwidth x17 over a decade = 4.7x, so the ridge climbs about fivefold (ch06's figures)
Link 1 icon: arrows to scale, amber 120 px vs coral 120 x 17/80 = 25.5 px (about a fifth)
Link 2: 70 billion weights x 2 bytes = 140 GB per token
Link 3: decode pays the full read every token: 140 GB / 4.8 TB/s = 29.2 ms on an H200
Link 4: KV cache per token 2 x 80 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 327,680 bytes, about 320 KB
Road ahead, slot A (ch12's raise-bandwidth example): H200 4.8 TB/s / 140 GB = 34 tokens/s
Road ahead, slot B (ch12): 8-bit weights halve 140 GB to 70 GB; 3.35 TB/s / 70 GB = about 48 tokens/s
Road ahead, slot C (ch12): 10 requests sharing one read of the weights = about 240 tokens/s in all, each user still about 24 (weights only)
Road ahead, card 8 tag '> 99% idle at batch 1': 1 - 1/ridge = 99.7% on an H100, 99.5% on an H200
